the total capacity of a complex Gaussian multiple-access system can be achieved by a successive decoding equalizer, and that this equalizer involves no feedback equalization for the conventional GMAC.

multiuser coding for the complex GMAC.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OSD achieves any rate-tuple on the capacity region of a complex Gaussian GMAC with any product input distribution.
the OSD achieves total capacity for any vertex of the GMAC capacity region and has a complexity that is linear in the number N of users.
for the GMAC, successive decoding is optimum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OSD achieves all the capacity of the GMOC at any rate-tuple, and it is optimum for uncoded transmission.
the OSD achieves total capacity at the capacity vertices for the Gaussian multiple-access and broadcast channels.

the OSD is optimum in the following three senses: (i) it maximizes mutual information; (ii) it maximizes signal to interference; and (iii) it achieves the total capacity at any vertex of capacity region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
successive decoding with equalization achieves the total capacity for the complex GMAC.
the OSD is a practical, low-complexity, and near-capacity multiuser receiver for the GMAC.
the OSD is a good approximation to optimum joint decoding for the GMAC.
